decisions.choice: all the words: the message of 42:9-22, which the people had asked for and promised to obey
decisions.reason: The leaders had begged Jeremiah to ask the LORD where they should go and had sworn to do whatever he said (42:1-6). The answer was to stay in the land and not go to Egypt (42:10-19). The verse stresses that Jeremiah left nothing out: he spoke "all the words", "all these words".

decisions.choice: when Jeremiah had finished: a time clause leading into the leaders' reply in verse 2
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on in verse 2, where the leaders answer as soon as he stops speaking. The same opening is used when the crowd seized Jeremiah after his temple sermon (26:8).

decisions.choice: the LORD their God had sent him: Jeremiah is a true messenger
decisions.reason: The repeated "the LORD their God" and "had sent him" prepare for the charge of verse 2, "the LORD our God did not send you". The narrator has already said that he was sent.

decisions.choice: a full sentence at Readable
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's time clause running on into verse 2; Readable makes it a sentence of its own and starts verse 2 with "Then".

decisions.choice: the arrogant men: men who set themselves against God's word in pride
decisions.reason: The word describes people who act presumptuously, refusing to be told (Deuteronomy 17:12-13; 18:22; Psalm 119:21). The narrator judges the speakers before they speak: their answer is pride, not doubt.

decisions.choice: falsehood: the charge Jeremiah had made against the false prophets is turned against him
decisions.reason: *Sheqer*, "falsehood, lie", is the book's word for the message of the false prophets (14:14; 23:25-26; 27:10-16). Now the leaders use it of the LORD's own word.

decisions.choice: Azariah son of Hoshaiah: probably the same man as Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah in 42:1
decisions.reason: 42:1 names Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah with Johanan; here the Hebrew has Azariah. The Greek translation reads Azariah in both places. Either the man had two names or one name was changed in copying; the Hebrew of each verse is followed. This description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: to sojourn there: to settle in Egypt as people living away from their own land
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 42:15-22 for going to live in Egypt as outsiders. It is the very thing the LORD had forbidden.

decisions.choice: settle (Balanced), live (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sojourn"; Balanced and Readable use everyday words for going to live in another land.

decisions.choice: the forbidden words given indirectly at Readable
decisions.reason: Readable reports the command "Do not go to Egypt" without a quotation inside the quotation. The leaders' speech continues into verse 3.

decisions.choice: Mentira dices (L); es mentira (B); Estás mintiendo (R)
decisions.reason: *Sheqer* is "mentira" in this translation; the men turn the prophet's own charge against him.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}}
decisions.reason: The forbidden words quoted are spoken to the people as a whole, so they take the plural_you span; Readable reports them without one.

decisions.choice: "uongo" at every level
decisions.reason: The word set for *sheqer* in Swahili Jeremiah; here the leaders turn against Jeremiah the charge he had made against the false prophets.

decisions.choice: điều giả dối (L); nói dối (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word *sheqer*, set as "sự giả dối, lời giả dối" for these books, is here thrown back at the prophet; Balanced and Readable say it as a plain accusation.

decisions.choice: The leaders now answer Jeremiah in 하오체 ("거짓을 말하고 있소"), dropping the 합쇼체 of their request (42:2)
decisions.reason: The change of speech level marks their turn against the prophet without making them openly insolent; they still speak of God with "-시-".

decisions.choice: "거짓" (L), "거짓말" (B, R) for *sheqer*
decisions.reason: The terms note's word: the charge Jeremiah made against the false prophets is turned against him.

decisions.choice: falsidade (L); mentira (B); Você está mentindo (R)
decisions.reason: Sheqer, the book's word for the false prophets' message (m2), is "falsidade" at Literal, as the English "falsehood", and "mentira" at Balanced and Readable, as the English "lie"; the leaders now turn it on the LORD's own word. "Azarias" is kept as the Hebrew has it here (m3).

ko.B: 네리야의 아들 바룩이 당신을 부추겨 우리를 해치려는 것이오. 우리를 갈대아 사람들에게 넘겨주어, 죽게 하거나 바빌론으로 끌려가게 하려는 것이오."
ko.R: 네리야의 아들 바룩이 당신을 부추겨서 우리에게 맞서게 하고 있소. 그는 우리가 바빌로니아 사람들에게 넘겨지기를 바라오. 그래서 그들이 우리를 죽이거나 바빌론으로 포로로 끌고 가게 하려는 것이오."

pt.L: Mas Baruque, filho de Nerias, está incitando você contra nós, para nos entregar na mão dos caldeus, para nos matar ou nos levar para o exílio [na] Babilônia."
pt.B: Quem está instigando você contra nós é Baruque, filho de Nerias, para que sejamos entregues aos caldeus, para sermos mortos ou levados para a Babilônia."
pt.R: É Baruque, filho de Nerias, que está pondo você contra nós. Ele quer que sejamos entregues aos babilônios, para que eles nos matem ou nos levem como prisioneiros para a Babilônia."

decisions.choice: Baruch son of Neriah: Jeremiah's scribe and companion
decisions.reason: Baruch wrote down Jeremiah's words and read them in the temple (32:12; 36:4-10). The leaders cannot say that Jeremiah himself is lying for no reason, so they blame his helper, as though Baruch had put the words in his mouth.

decisions.choice: inciting: urging someone on against another
decisions.reason: The verb is used of stirring a person up to act (1 Samuel 26:19; 1 Kings 21:25). They accuse Baruch of working on Jeremiah to set him against them.

decisions.choice: to be killed or exiled: the very fear that had made them want to flee
decisions.reason: After Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, the governor appointed by Babylon, the leaders feared the Chaldeans would punish them (41:18; 42:11-16). They now say that staying in Judah, as the LORD told them, is a trap set by Baruch.

decisions.choice: Babylonians
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Jeremiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans, the people who ruled Babylon.

decisions.choice: or
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the two fates with "and"; here it means one or the other, so every level says "or".

source.text: וְלֹֽא־שָׁמַע֩ יוֹחָנָ֨ן בֶּן־קָרֵ֜חַ וְכָל־שָׂרֵ֧י הַחֲיָלִ֛ים וְכָל־הָעָ֖ם בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not listened Johanan son of Kareah and all [the] commanders of the forces and all the people to [the] voice of Yahweh, to remain in [the] land of Judah.

en.L: And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces and all the people did not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to remain in the land of Judah.
en.B: So Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces and all the people refused to obey the command {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them to remain in the land of Judah.
en.R: Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders and all the people refused to obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He had told them to stay in the land of Judah.

es.L: Y no escucharon Johanán hijo de Carea, y todos los jefes de las tropas, y todo el pueblo, la voz {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de quedarse en la tierra de Judá.
es.B: Así que Johanán hijo de Carea, todos los jefes de las tropas y todo el pueblo se negaron a obedecer la orden que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dio de quedarse en la tierra de Judá.
es.R: Johanán hijo de Carea, todos los jefes del ejército y todo el pueblo se negaron a obedecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Él les había dicho que se quedaran en la tierra de Judá.

fr.L: Et Yohanân fils de Qaréah, et tous les chefs des troupes, et tout le peuple n’écoutèrent pas la voix {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, [qui leur disait] de demeurer dans le pays de Juda.
fr.B: Ainsi Yohanân fils de Qaréah, tous les chefs des troupes et tout le peuple refusèrent d’obéir à l’ordre que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur avait donné de demeurer dans le pays de Juda.
fr.R: Yohanân fils de Qaréah, tous les chefs de l’armée et tout le peuple ont refusé d’obéir {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Il leur avait dit de rester dans le pays de Juda.

sw.L: Basi Yohana mwana wa Karea na wakuu wote wa majeshi na watu wote hawakuisikiliza sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kukaa katika nchi ya Yuda.
sw.B: Basi Yohana mwana wa Karea, wakuu wote wa majeshi na watu wote walikataa kuitii amri ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwapa ya kukaa katika nchi ya Yuda.
sw.R: Yohana mwana wa Karea, makamanda wote wa jeshi na watu wote walikataa kumtii {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Yeye alikuwa amewaambia wakae katika nchi ya Yuda.

vi.L: Giô-ha-nan con trai Ca-rê-át, tất cả các tướng chỉ huy quân lính và cả dân chúng không nghe theo tiếng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} để ở lại trong xứ Giu-đa.
vi.B: Vậy Giô-ha-nan con trai Ca-rê-át, tất cả các tướng chỉ huy quân lính và cả dân chúng không chịu vâng theo mệnh lệnh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} truyền cho họ ở lại trong xứ Giu-đa.
vi.R: Giô-ha-nan con trai Ca-rê-át, tất cả các tướng chỉ huy quân đội và cả dân chúng không chịu vâng lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Ngài đã bảo họ ở lại trong xứ Giu-đa.

ko.L: 그리고 가레아의 아들 요하난과 모든 군대 지휘관과 모든 백성이 유다 땅에 머무르라는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 목소리를 듣지 않았다.
ko.B: 이렇게 가레아의 아들 요하난과 모든 군대 지휘관과 모든 백성은 유다 땅에 머무르라고 하신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 명령에 순종하지 않았다.
ko.R: 가레아의 아들 요하난과 모든 군대 지휘관과 모든 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 순종하지 않았다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들에게 유다 땅에 머무르라고 말씀하셨다.

pt.L: E Joanã, filho de Careá, e todos os chefes das tropas, e todo o povo não ouviram a voz {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, de permanecer na terra de Judá.
pt.B: Assim Joanã, filho de Careá, todos os comandantes das tropas e todo o povo se recusaram a obedecer à ordem {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} de permanecer na terra de Judá.
pt.R: Joanã, filho de Careá, todos os comandantes do exército e todo o povo se recusaram a obedecer {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Ele tinha mandado que ficassem na terra de Judá.

decisions.choice: did not listen to the voice of the LORD: they disobeyed his command
decisions.reason: "Listening to the voice" of someone means obeying them. It is the very thing they had promised in 42:6: "we will listen to the voice of the LORD our God".

decisions.choice: the commanders of the forces: the officers of the Judean troops still in the land
decisions.reason: They had gathered to Gedaliah after the fall of Jerusalem (40:7-8, 13; 2 Kings 25:23), and Johanan had led them against Ishmael (41:11-16).

decisions.choice: He had told them
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that staying in Judah was what the LORD had commanded.

decisions.choice: army commanders
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:23, Readable says "army commanders" for "commanders of the forces".

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֞ח יוֹחָנָ֤ן בֶּן־קָרֵ֨חַ֙ וְכָל־שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים אֵ֖ת כָּל־שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֗בוּ מִכָּל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִדְּחוּ־שָׁ֔ם לָג֖וּר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Johanan son of Kareah and all [the] commanders of the forces all [the] remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been driven there, to sojourn in [the] land of Judah:

en.L: And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been driven, to sojourn in the land of Judah:
en.B: But Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces led away the whole remnant of Judah, those who had come back from all the nations where they had been scattered in order to live in the land of Judah:
en.R: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders took with them everyone who was left from Judah. This included the people who had come back to live in Judah from all the countries where they had been scattered.

es.L: Y tomaron Johanán hijo de Carea y todos los jefes de las tropas a todo el remanente de Judá que había vuelto de todas las naciones adonde habían sido arrojados, para residir en la tierra de Judá:
es.B: Pero Johanán hijo de Carea y todos los jefes de las tropas se llevaron a todo el remanente de Judá, a los que habían regresado de todas las naciones por donde habían sido dispersados para vivir en la tierra de Judá:
es.R: Johanán hijo de Carea y todos los jefes del ejército se llevaron a todos los que habían quedado de Judá. Entre ellos estaban los que habían vuelto a vivir en Judá desde todos los países por donde habían sido dispersados.

fr.L: Et Yohanân fils de Qaréah et tous les chefs des troupes prirent tout le reste de Juda qui était revenu de toutes les nations où ils avaient été chassés, pour séjourner dans le pays de Juda :
fr.B: Mais Yohanân fils de Qaréah et tous les chefs des troupes emmenèrent tout le reste de Juda, ceux qui étaient revenus de toutes les nations où ils avaient été dispersés pour habiter dans le pays de Juda :
fr.R: Yohanân fils de Qaréah et tous les chefs de l’armée ont emmené avec eux tous ceux qui restaient de Juda. Parmi eux, il y avait les gens qui étaient revenus vivre en Juda de tous les pays où ils avaient été dispersés.

sw.L: Bali Yohana mwana wa Karea na wakuu wote wa majeshi wakawachukua mabaki yote ya Yuda waliorudi kutoka mataifa yote walikofukuzwa, ili kukaa katika nchi ya Yuda:
sw.B: Lakini Yohana mwana wa Karea na wakuu wote wa majeshi waliwachukua mabaki yote ya Yuda, wale waliokuwa wamerudi kutoka mataifa yote walikotawanywa ili waishi katika nchi ya Yuda:
sw.R: Yohana mwana wa Karea na makamanda wote wa jeshi waliwachukua pamoja nao watu wote waliobaki kutoka Yuda. Kati yao walikuwa watu waliokuwa wamerudi kuishi Yuda kutoka nchi zote walikokuwa wametawanywa.

vi.L: Giô-ha-nan con trai Ca-rê-át và tất cả các tướng chỉ huy quân lính đem theo tất cả những người sót lại của Giu-đa, là những người đã từ mọi dân tộc, nơi họ bị đuổi đến, trở về kiều ngụ trong xứ Giu-đa:
vi.B: Nhưng Giô-ha-nan con trai Ca-rê-át và tất cả các tướng chỉ huy quân lính dẫn đi tất cả những người sót lại của Giu-đa, là những người đã từ mọi dân tộc nơi họ bị tản lạc trở về sống trong xứ Giu-đa:
vi.R: Giô-ha-nan con trai Ca-rê-át và tất cả các tướng chỉ huy quân đội đem theo mọi người còn lại của Giu-đa. Trong số đó có những người đã từ mọi nước nơi họ bị tản lạc trở về sống ở Giu-đa.

ko.L: 그리고 가레아의 아들 요하난과 모든 군대 지휘관이, 쫓겨 갔던 모든 민족에게서 유다 땅에 살려고 돌아온 유다의 남은 자들을 모두 데려갔다.
ko.B: 그러나 가레아의 아들 요하난과 모든 군대 지휘관은 유다의 남은 사람들을 모두 데리고 갔다. 그들은 흩어져 있던 모든 나라에서 유다 땅에 살려고 돌아온 사람들이었다.
ko.R: 가레아의 아들 요하난과 모든 군대 지휘관은 유다에 남아 있던 사람들을 모두 데리고 갔다. 거기에는 여러 나라에 흩어져 있다가 유다에서 살려고 돌아온 사람들도 있었다.

pt.L: E Joanã, filho de Careá, e todos os chefes das tropas tomaram todo o remanescente de Judá que tinha voltado de todas as nações para onde tinham sido expulsos, para morar como estrangeiros na terra de Judá:
pt.B: Mas Joanã, filho de Careá, e todos os comandantes das tropas levaram todo o remanescente de Judá, os que tinham voltado de todas as nações por onde tinham sido espalhados, para viver na terra de Judá:
pt.R: Joanã, filho de Careá, e todos os comandantes do exército levaram com eles todos os que tinham restado de Judá. Entre eles estavam as pessoas que tinham voltado para morar em Judá, vindas de todos os países por onde tinham sido espalhadas.

decisions.choice: the remnant of Judah: those left in the land after the exile to Babylon
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had called them "the remnant of Judah" in 42:15, 19. Their going down to Egypt undoes the return described in 40:11-12, when Judeans scattered in Moab, Ammon and Edom came back to Gedaliah.

decisions.choice: who had returned from all the nations: the Judeans who had fled during the war and came back
decisions.reason: 40:11-12 tells how they returned and gathered a large harvest. The word "driven" is used elsewhere of Israel scattered in judgment (8:3; 16:15).

decisions.choice: to sojourn in the land of Judah: they had come back to live in their own land
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 2 now describes living in Judah. Those who had come back to make a home in the land are taken away from it again.

decisions.choice: scattered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "scattered" for "driven away"; the picture is of people forced to flee in many directions.

source.text: אֶֽת־הַ֠גְּבָרִים וְאֶת־הַנָּשִׁ֣ים וְאֶת־הַטַּף֮ וְאֶת־בְּנ֣וֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־הַנֶּ֗פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִנִּ֨יחַ֙ נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֣ן רַב־טַבָּחִ֔ים אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אֲחִיקָ֣ם בֶּן־שָׁפָ֑ן וְאֵת֙ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא וְאֶת־בָּר֖וּךְ בֶּן־נֵרִיָּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: the men and the women and the little ones and [the] daughters of the king, and every person whom had left Nebuzaradan chief of [the] guards with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.

en.L: the men and the women and the little ones and the daughters of the king, and every person whom Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
en.B: the men, the women and the children, the king's daughters, and everyone whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and also the prophet Jeremiah and Baruch son of Neriah.
en.R: They took men, women and children, and the king's daughters. They took everyone that Nebuzaradan, the commander of the royal guard, had left in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and grandson of Shaphan. They also took the prophet Jeremiah and Baruch son of Neriah.

es.L: a los hombres, y a las mujeres, y a los niños, y a las hijas del rey, y a toda persona que Nabuzaradán, jefe de la guardia, había dejado con Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, y a Jeremías el profeta y a Baruc hijo de Nerías.
es.B: hombres, mujeres y niños, las hijas del rey, y todos los que Nabuzaradán, capitán de la guardia, había dejado con Gedalías hijo de Ahicam, hijo de Safán, y también al profeta Jeremías y a Baruc hijo de Nerías.
es.R: Se llevaron a hombres, mujeres y niños, y a las hijas del rey. Se llevaron a todos los que Nabuzaradán, el comandante de la guardia real, había dejado al cuidado de Gedalías hijo de Ahicam y nieto de Safán. También se llevaron al profeta Jeremías y a Baruc hijo de Nerías.

fr.L: les hommes, et les femmes, et les enfants, et les filles du roi, et toute personne que Nebouzaradân, chef des gardes, avait laissée avec Guedalia fils d’Ahiqam, fils de Shaphân, et Jérémie le prophète et Baruch fils de Nériya.
fr.B: les hommes, les femmes et les enfants, les filles du roi, et tous ceux que Nebouzaradân, le commandant de la garde, avait laissés avec Guedalia fils d’Ahiqam, fils de Shaphân, ainsi que le prophète Jérémie et Baruch fils de Nériya.
fr.R: Ils ont emmené des hommes, des femmes et des enfants, et les filles du roi. Ils ont emmené tous ceux que Nebouzaradân, le chef de la garde royale, avait confiés à Guedalia fils d’Ahiqam et petit-fils de Shaphân. Ils ont emmené aussi le prophète Jérémie et Baruch fils de Nériya.

sw.L: wanaume na wanawake na watoto na binti za mfalme, na kila mtu ambaye Nebuzaradani mkuu wa walinzi alimwacha pamoja na Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu mwana wa Shafani, na Yeremia nabii na Baruku mwana wa Neria.
sw.B: wanaume, wanawake na watoto, binti za mfalme, na kila mtu ambaye Nebuzaradani kamanda wa walinzi alikuwa amemwacha pamoja na Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu, mwana wa Shafani, na pia nabii Yeremia na Baruku mwana wa Neria.
sw.R: Waliwachukua wanaume, wanawake na watoto, na binti za mfalme. Walimchukua kila mtu ambaye Nebuzaradani, kamanda wa walinzi wa mfalme, alikuwa amemwacha chini ya uangalizi wa Gedalia mwana wa Ahikamu na mjukuu wa Shafani. Walimchukua pia nabii Yeremia na Baruku mwana wa Neria.

vi.L: đàn ông, đàn bà, trẻ nhỏ, các con gái của vua, và mọi người mà Nê-bu-xa-a-đan, quan chỉ huy vệ binh, đã để lại với Ghê-đa-lia con trai A-hi-cam, con trai Sa-phan, cùng nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi và Ba-rúc con trai Nê-ri-gia.
vi.B: đàn ông, đàn bà và trẻ con, các công chúa, và mọi người mà Nê-bu-xa-a-đan, quan chỉ huy đội cận vệ, đã để lại với Ghê-đa-lia con trai A-hi-cam, cháu Sa-phan, cùng với nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi và Ba-rúc con trai Nê-ri-gia.
vi.R: Họ đem theo đàn ông, đàn bà, trẻ con và các công chúa. Họ đem theo mọi người mà Nê-bu-xa-a-đan, người chỉ huy đội cận vệ hoàng gia, đã giao cho Ghê-đa-lia con trai A-hi-cam, cháu Sa-phan, coi sóc. Họ cũng đem theo nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi và Ba-rúc con trai Nê-ri-gia.

ko.L: 곧 남자들과 여자들과 어린아이들과 왕의 딸들과, 경호대장 느부사라단이 사반의 손자 아히감의 아들 그다랴에게 남겨 둔 모든 사람과, 예언자 예레미야와 네리야의 아들 바룩이었다.
ko.B: 그들은 남자와 여자와 아이들과 왕의 딸들과, 경호대장 느부사라단이 사반의 손자요 아히감의 아들인 그다랴에게 맡겨 둔 모든 사람이었다. 예언자 예레미야와 네리야의 아들 바룩도 데리고 갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 남자와 여자와 아이들과 왕의 딸들을 데리고 갔다. 왕의 경호대장 느부사라단이 사반의 손자요 아히감의 아들인 그다랴에게 맡겨 두었던 모든 사람을 데리고 갔다. 예언자 예레미야와 네리야의 아들 바룩도 데리고 갔다.

pt.L: os homens, e as mulheres, e as crianças, e as filhas do rei, e toda pessoa que Nebuzaradã, o chefe da guarda, tinha deixado com Gedalias, filho de Aicam, filho de Safã, e Jeremias, o profeta, e Baruque, filho de Nerias.
pt.B: os homens, as mulheres e as crianças, as filhas do rei e todos os que Nebuzaradã, capitão da guarda, tinha deixado com Gedalias, filho de Aicam, filho de Safã, e também o profeta Jeremias e Baruque, filho de Nerias.
pt.R: Levaram homens, mulheres e crianças, e as filhas do rei. Levaram todos os que Nebuzaradã, o comandante da guarda real, tinha deixado aos cuidados de Gedalias, filho de Aicam e neto de Safã. Levaram também o profeta Jeremias e Baruque, filho de Nerias.

decisions.choice: the king's daughters: women of the royal family, probably Zedekiah's
decisions.reason: They were left in the land when Zedekiah was captured (39:6-7; 41:10). "Daughters of the king" may also mean royal women more broadly.

decisions.choice: Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard: the Babylonian commander who carried out the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: He burned the city and took its people into exile, and he left the poorest in the land under Gedaliah (39:9-10; 40:7; 2 Kings 25:8-12, 22).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch: taken along against the word they had brought
decisions.reason: The list ends with the two men whose message was refused. Jeremiah goes into Egypt with the people he had warned not to go.

decisions.choice: chief of the guard (Literal), captain of the guard (Balanced), commander of the royal guard (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 25:8.

decisions.choice: everyone
decisions.reason: *Nefesh*, "person, soul", here simply means each person; "everyone" already includes men and women.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֛י לֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־תַּחְפַּנְחֵֽס׃ס

en.L: And they came [into the] land of Egypt, because they did not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
en.B: So they went into the land of Egypt, since they did not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and came as far as Tahpanhes.
en.R: They went into Egypt, because they would not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They traveled as far as the town of Tahpanhes.

es.L: Y entraron en la tierra de Egipto, porque no escucharon la voz {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y llegaron hasta Tafnes.
es.B: Así entraron en la tierra de Egipto, porque no obedecieron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y llegaron hasta Tafnes.
es.R: Se fueron a Egipto, porque no quisieron obedecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Viajaron hasta la ciudad de Tafnes.

fr.L: Et ils entrèrent [au] pays d’Égypte, car ils n’écoutèrent pas la voix {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et ils arrivèrent jusqu’à Tahpanhès.
fr.B: Ils entrèrent donc au pays d’Égypte, puisqu’ils n’avaient pas obéi {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, et ils arrivèrent jusqu’à Tahpanhès.
fr.R: Ils sont entrés en Égypte, parce qu’ils n’ont pas voulu obéir {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. Ils sont allés jusqu’à la ville de Tahpanhès.

sw.L: Wakaingia [katika] nchi ya Misri, kwa sababu hawakuisikiliza sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; wakafika mpaka Tahpanhesi.
sw.B: Basi wakaingia katika nchi ya Misri, kwa kuwa hawakumtii {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakafika mpaka Tahpanhesi.
sw.R: Waliingia Misri, kwa sababu hawakutaka kumtii {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wakasafiri mpaka mji wa Tahpanhesi.

vi.L: Họ đi vào xứ Ai Cập, vì họ không nghe theo tiếng của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; và họ đến tận Tác-pha-nết.
vi.B: Vậy họ đi vào xứ Ai Cập, vì họ không vâng lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và đến tận Tác-pha-nết.
vi.R: Họ đi vào Ai Cập, vì họ không chịu vâng lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ đi đến tận thành Tác-pha-nết.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 목소리를 듣지 않았으므로 이집트 땅으로 들어가 다바네스까지 이르렀다.
ko.B: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 순종하지 않고 이집트 땅으로 들어가, 다바네스까지 갔다.
ko.R: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 순종하지 않고 이집트로 들어갔다. 그리고 다바네스 성읍까지 갔다.

pt.L: E entraram na terra do Egito, porque não ouviram a voz {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; e chegaram até Tafnes.
pt.B: Assim eles foram para a terra do Egito, pois não obedeceram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, e chegaram até Tafnes.
pt.R: Eles foram para o Egito, porque não quiseram obedecer {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}. Viajaram até a cidade de Tafnes.

decisions.choice: Tahpanhes: a fortress town on Egypt's eastern border, in the Nile Delta
decisions.reason: It was one of the first Egyptian towns a traveler from Judah would reach (2:16; 44:1; 46:14). Greek writers called it Daphnae.

decisions.choice: because they did not listen: the narrator repeats the reason from verse 4
decisions.reason: The repeated words make the going down to Egypt itself the act of disobedience. Going back to Egypt reverses the exodus, which the Law had forbidden (Deuteronomy 17:16).

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says that Tahpanhes is a town.

decisions.choice: Tafnes
decisions.reason: The form set for Tahpanhes, a fortress town on Egypt's eastern border.

decisions.choice: Tác-pha-nết
decisions.reason: A new place name; the form follows the terms note.

decisions.choice: "다바네스"
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for Tahpanhes.

decisions.choice: Tafnes
decisions.reason: For the whole book (2:16; 44:1; 46:14): the town (m1) is "Tafnes", the usual Brazilian form of the name, as the shared rules for Jeremiah set it; the Greek name Daphnae is left to the notes.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came in Tahpanhes: God still speaks to his prophet in Egypt
decisions.reason: Leaving the land has not taken the people beyond the LORD's reach. The message that follows answers their hope of safety in Egypt (42:14).

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying: (Literal); ... came to Jeremiah: (Balanced); the LORD gave Jeremiah this message (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's formula for the word coming to the prophet, as in 28:12.

source.text: קַ֣ח בְּיָדְךָ֞ אֲבָנִ֣ים גְּדֹל֗וֹת וּטְמַנְתָּ֤ם בַּמֶּ֨לֶט֙ בַּמַּלְבֵּ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּפֶ֥תַח בֵּית־פַּרְעֹ֖ה בְּתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס לְעֵינֵ֖י אֲנָשִׁ֥ים יְהוּדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Take in your hand stones large, and hide them in the mortar in the brick-terrace which [is] at [the] entrance of [the] house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, to [the] eyes of men Judeans,

en.L: "Take large stones in your hand, and hide them in the mortar in the brick terrace that [is] at the entrance of the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, before the eyes of Judean men,
en.B: "Take some large stones in your hands and bury them in the mortar of the brick pavement at the entrance of Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes, while the men of Judah watch.
en.R: "Pick up some large stones. While the men from Judah are watching, hide them in the clay of the brick pavement by the doorway of Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes.

es.L: «Toma en tu mano piedras grandes y escóndelas en la argamasa del enladrillado que [está] a la entrada de la casa del faraón en Tafnes, a la vista de hombres judíos,
es.B: «Toma en tus manos unas piedras grandes y entiérralas en la argamasa del pavimento de ladrillos que está a la entrada del palacio del faraón en Tafnes, mientras los hombres de Judá miran.
es.R: «Toma unas piedras grandes. Mientras los hombres de Judá están mirando, escóndelas en el barro del pavimento de ladrillos, junto a la puerta del palacio del faraón en Tafnes.

fr.L: « Prends dans ta main de grandes pierres, et cache-les dans le mortier, dans la terrasse de briques qui [est] à l’entrée de la maison du pharaon, à Tahpanhès, sous les yeux d’hommes judéens,
fr.B: « Prends dans tes mains de grandes pierres et enfouis-les dans le mortier du pavement de briques, à l’entrée du palais du pharaon à Tahpanhès, sous les yeux des hommes de Juda.
fr.R: « Ramasse de grosses pierres. Pendant que les hommes de Juda te regardent, cache-les dans l’argile du pavement de briques, devant la porte du palais du pharaon à Tahpanhès.

sw.L: "Chukua mawe makubwa mkononi mwako, uyafiche katika chokaa katika sakafu ya matofali iliyoko penye mlango wa nyumba ya Farao huko Tahpanhesi, mbele ya macho ya watu wa Kiyahudi,
sw.B: "Chukua mawe makubwa mikononi mwako, uyazike katika chokaa ya sakafu ya matofali penye mlango wa ikulu ya Farao huko Tahpanhesi, watu wa Yuda wakitazama.
sw.R: "Chukua mawe makubwa. Watu wa Yuda wakiwa wanatazama, yafiche katika udongo wa sakafu ya matofali karibu na mlango wa ikulu ya Farao huko Tahpanhesi.

vi.L: "Hãy lấy trong tay ngươi những tảng đá lớn và giấu chúng trong vữa của nền gạch ở lối vào cung Pha-ra-ôn tại Tác-pha-nết, trước mắt những người Giu-đa,
vi.B: "Con hãy lấy vài tảng đá lớn và chôn chúng trong vữa của sân lát gạch ở lối vào cung điện Pha-ra-ôn tại Tác-pha-nết, trong khi những người Giu-đa đứng xem.
vi.R: "Con hãy nhặt vài tảng đá lớn. Trong khi những người Giu-đa đứng xem, hãy giấu chúng trong lớp đất sét của sân lát gạch cạnh cửa cung điện Pha-ra-ôn tại Tác-pha-nết.

ko.L: "너는 손에 큰 돌들을 들고, 유다 사람들의 눈앞에서 다바네스에 있는 바로의 집 입구의 벽돌 깐 곳에 있는 진흙 속에 그것들을 숨겨라.
ko.B: "너는 큰 돌 몇 개를 들고, 유다 사람들이 보는 앞에서 다바네스에 있는 바로의 궁전 입구, 벽돌을 깐 마당의 흙 속에 그것들을 묻어라.
ko.R: "큰 돌을 몇 개 집어 들어라. 그리고 유다 사람들이 보고 있을 때, 다바네스에 있는 바로의 궁전 문 앞, 벽돌을 깐 바닥의 흙 속에 그 돌들을 숨겨라.

pt.L: "Toma pedras grandes na tua mão e esconde-as na argamassa, no terraço de tijolos que [está] à entrada da casa de Faraó, em Tafnes, diante dos olhos de homens judeus,
pt.B: "Pega algumas pedras grandes com as mãos e enterra-as na argamassa do pavimento de tijolos, à entrada do palácio de Faraó, em Tafnes, enquanto os homens de Judá olham.
pt.R: "Pega algumas pedras grandes. Enquanto os homens de Judá estiverem olhando, esconde as pedras no barro do pavimento de tijolos, perto da porta do palácio de Faraó, em Tafnes.

decisions.choice: mortar: probably the clay or mortar that bound the bricks
alternatives: secretly (taking the letters as a different phrase)
decisions.reason: The word appears only here in the Bible, and its meaning is guessed from related words in other languages, which point to clay or mortar.

decisions.choice: brick terrace: a paved area or platform of bricks in front of the building
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the word means a brick mold or brick kiln (2 Samuel 12:31; Nahum 3:14). Here it seems to be brickwork at the entrance. A large brick platform found at the site of Tahpanhes has been linked with this verse, though the link is not certain.

decisions.choice: the house of Pharaoh: a royal building in Tahpanhes
decisions.reason: The king of Egypt at this time was Pharaoh Hophra (44:30). A border fortress town could have a royal residence or government house used by the king or his officials.

decisions.choice: an acted message, done where Judeans can see it
decisions.reason: Like the linen belt (13:1-11), the broken jar (19:1-13) and the yoke (27:2), the buried stones are a sign that the watching men of Judah are meant to remember when the message comes true.

decisions.choice: brick pavement; Pharaoh's palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for the brickwork and for the royal building, which Literal calls "the house of Pharaoh".

decisions.choice: "While the men from Judah are watching" placed first
decisions.reason: Readable puts the witnesses first so the long sentence can be broken into two short ones.

decisions.choice: a casa de Faraó (L); o palácio de Faraó (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Faraó" as a name, with no article, where the English says "Pharaoh" without one, as the Old Testament terms set it; Balanced and Readable say "palácio" for the royal house (m3), as the English does. God speaks to Jeremiah with "tu".

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֡ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֤י שֹׁלֵ֨חַ֙ וְ֠לָקַחְתִּי אֶת־נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֤ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ עַבְדִּ֔י וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י כִסְא֔וֹ מִמַּ֛עַל לָאֲבָנִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֣ר טָמָ֑נְתִּי וְנָטָ֥ה אֶת־שַׁפְרִיר֖וֹ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and you shall say to them, Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Behold I [am] sending, and I will take Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon my servant, and I will set his throne above the stones the these which I have hidden, and he will spread his canopy over them.

en.L: and say to them, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am sending, and I will take Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.
en.B: Then tell them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I am about to send for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, and bring him here. I will set his throne over these stones that I have buried, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.
en.R: Then tell them, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to send for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. He is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, and I will bring him here. I will set up his throne on top of these stones I have hidden. He will spread his royal tent over them.

es.L: y diles: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: He aquí, yo envío y tomaré a Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, y pondré su trono sobre estas piedras que he escondido, y él extenderá su dosel real sobre ellas.
es.B: Luego diles: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: Voy a mandar a buscar a Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, y lo traeré aquí. Pondré su trono sobre estas piedras que he enterrado, y él extenderá su dosel real sobre ellas.
es.R: Luego diles: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: Voy a mandar a buscar a Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia. Él es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo, y lo traeré aquí. Pondré su trono encima de estas piedras que he escondido. Él extenderá sobre ellas su tienda real.

fr.L: et dis-leur : “Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : Voici, j’envoie, et je prendrai Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, et je placerai son trône au-dessus de ces pierres que j’ai cachées, et il déploiera sur elles son dais royal.
fr.B: Puis dis-leur : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : Je vais envoyer chercher Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, et je le ferai venir. Je placerai son trône sur ces pierres que j’ai enfouies, et il déploiera sur elles son dais royal.
fr.R: Ensuite dis-leur : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : Je vais envoyer chercher Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone. C’est {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, et je le ferai venir ici. J’installerai son trône sur ces pierres que j’ai cachées. Il dressera sa tente royale au-dessus d’elles.

sw.L: kisha uwaambie, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi, Mungu wa Israeli: Tazama, ninatuma, nami nitamtwaa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, nami nitakiweka kiti chake cha enzi juu ya mawe haya niliyoyaficha, naye atatandika hema yake ya kifalme juu yake.
sw.B: Kisha uwaambie, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Ninakaribia kutuma kumwita Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, na kumleta hapa. Nitakiweka kiti chake cha enzi juu ya mawe haya niliyoyazika, naye atatandika hema yake ya kifalme juu yake.
sw.R: Kisha uwaambie, 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Nitatuma kumwita Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli. Yeye ni mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, nami nitamleta hapa. Nitakiweka kiti chake cha enzi juu ya mawe haya niliyoyaficha. Atatandika hema yake ya kifalme juu yake.

vi.L: và nói với họ: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán thế này: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai người đi đem Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đến, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đặt ngai nó trên những tảng đá {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giấu này, và nó sẽ giăng trướng hoàng gia của mình trên chúng.
vi.B: Rồi hãy nói với họ: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp sai người đi đón Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đem đến đây. Ta sẽ đặt ngai nó trên những tảng đá {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chôn này, và nó sẽ giăng trướng hoàng gia của mình trên đó.
vi.R: Rồi hãy nói với họ: 'Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai người đi đón Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn. Nó là đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đem nó đến đây. Ta sẽ đặt ngai nó trên những tảng đá {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giấu này. Nó sẽ giăng lều hoàng gia của mình trên đó.

ko.L: 그리고 그들에게 말하여라. '만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님께서 이와 같이 말씀하시오. 보라, 내가 사람을 보내어 나의 종 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살을 데려오겠다. 그리고 내가 숨긴 이 돌들 위에 그의 왕좌를 놓을 것이고, 그가 그것들 위에 그의 왕의 휘장을 펼칠 것이다.
ko.B: 그리고 그들에게 말하여라. '만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님께서 이렇게 말씀하시오. 내가 사람을 보내어 나의 종 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살을 이리로 데려오겠다. 내가 묻어 둔 이 돌들 위에 그의 왕좌를 놓겠고, 그는 그 위에 왕의 휘장을 펼칠 것이다.
ko.R: 그리고 그들에게 말하여라. '하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님께서 하시는 말씀이오. 내가 사람을 보내어 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살을 불러오겠다. 그는 나의 종이다. 내가 그를 이리로 데려오겠다. 내가 숨겨 둔 이 돌들 위에 그의 왕좌를 놓겠다. 그는 그 위에 왕의 천막을 칠 것이다.

pt.L: e dize-lhes: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel: Eis que eu envio e tomarei Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo, e porei o trono dele sobre estas pedras que escondi, e ele estenderá o seu dossel real sobre elas.
pt.B: Depois dize a eles: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel: Vou mandar buscar Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo, e trazê-lo aqui. Porei o trono dele sobre estas pedras que enterrei, e ele estenderá sobre elas o seu dossel real.
pt.R: Depois dize a eles: 'É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, diz: Vou mandar buscar Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia. Ele é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo, e eu vou trazê-lo aqui. Vou pôr o trono dele em cima destas pedras que escondi. Ele vai armar a sua tenda real sobre elas.

decisions.choice: my servant: Nebuchadrezzar as the one through whom God carries out his judgment
decisions.reason: As in 25:9 and 27:6, the title does not mean that the king worshiped Israel's God; it means he does God's work. The king the people fled from will follow them to Egypt at God's command.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the name used here
decisions.reason: Jeremiah usually spells the name Nebuchadrezzar, closer to the Babylonian Nabu-kudurri-usur; chapters 27-29 use Nebuchadnezzar (27:6). Both name the same king.

decisions.choice: I am sending and will take: I will send for him and bring him
decisions.reason: "Send and take" means to send for someone and have them brought (Genesis 27:45; 1 Samuel 16:11).

decisions.choice: I will set ... that I have hidden: the LORD speaks of the prophet's act and the king's act as his own
alternatives: he will set ... you have hidden
decisions.reason: Jeremiah buries the stones (verse 9), but God says "I have hidden"; the king sets up his throne, but God says "I will set". The Greek translation reads "he will set" and "you have hidden". The Hebrew is followed. This description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: royal canopy: a covering spread over the king's throne, perhaps a tent or a carpet
decisions.reason: The word appears only here, and its exact sense is uncertain. It is something of the king's that is stretched out over the place of his throne, a sign that he holds court and rules there.

decisions.choice: Look (Literal); left out at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: *Hinneh* points to what is about to happen; Balanced and Readable carry it with "I am about to" and "I am going to".

decisions.choice: the LORD's words in single quotation marks
decisions.reason: They are the message Jeremiah is to speak, inside the LORD's words to him, which opened in verse 9. The quotation runs to the end of verse 13.

decisions.choice: Nabucodorosor ... mi siervo
decisions.reason: "My servant": the foreign king serves God's purpose; the name keeps the r form the Hebrew has here.

decisions.choice: "mtumishi wangu" at every level for Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: God's servant is "mtumishi", never "mtumwa"; the word says the king carries out God's purpose without saying he worships him.

decisions.choice: đầy tớ của Ta (of Nebuchadrezzar)
decisions.reason: The terms note keeps "đầy tớ" for Nebuchadnezzar "my servant" at every level, as for the prophets. God speaks of the foreign king as "nó".

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's message to the Judeans in Egypt in his 하오체 ("말씀하시오"), God's words in 해라체, as at 42:9
decisions.reason: One register for Jeremiah's address to the people through chapters 42-44.

decisions.choice: "나의 종" for Nebuchadrezzar
decisions.reason: God names the king his servant as he names the prophets; the meaning decision explains the sense.

decisions.choice: Nabucodorosor
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew spells the king's name with "r" (m2), Portuguese writes "Nabucodorosor", as 21:7 does and as the English writes "Nebuchadrezzar"; "Nabucodonosor" where it spells it with "n". Both name the same king.

source.text: וּבָ֕א וְהִכָּ֖ה אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁ֧ר לַמָּ֣וֶת לַמָּ֗וֶת וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לַשְּׁבִי֙ לַשֶּׁ֔בִי וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לַחֶ֖רֶב לֶחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will come and strike [the] land of Egypt: who [are] for the death, to the death; and who [are] for the captivity, to the captivity; and who [are] for the sword, to the sword.

en.L: And he will come and strike the land of Egypt: those [who are] for death, to death; and those [who are] for captivity, to captivity; and those [who are] for the sword, to the sword.
en.B: He will come and strike the land of Egypt: whoever is marked out for death, to death; whoever is marked out for captivity, to captivity; and whoever is marked out for the sword, to the sword.
en.R: He will come and attack Egypt. Those who are meant to die will die. Those who are meant to be taken away as prisoners will be taken away. And those who are meant to be killed in war will be killed in war.

es.L: Y vendrá y herirá la tierra de Egipto: los [destinados] a la muerte, a la muerte; y los [destinados] al cautiverio, al cautiverio; y los [destinados] a la espada, a la espada.
es.B: Vendrá y herirá la tierra de Egipto: el que esté destinado a la muerte, a la muerte; el que esté destinado al cautiverio, al cautiverio; y el que esté destinado a la espada, a la espada.
es.R: Vendrá y atacará a Egipto. Los que tengan que morir, morirán. Los que tengan que ser llevados como prisioneros serán llevados. Y los que tengan que morir en la guerra morirán en la guerra.

fr.L: Et il viendra et frappera le pays d’Égypte : ceux [qui sont] pour la mort, à la mort ; et ceux [qui sont] pour la captivité, à la captivité ; et ceux [qui sont] pour l’épée, à l’épée.
fr.B: Il viendra frapper le pays d’Égypte : à la mort, qui est destiné à la mort ; à la captivité, qui est destiné à la captivité ; à l’épée, qui est destiné à l’épée.
fr.R: Il viendra attaquer l’Égypte. Ceux qui doivent mourir mourront. Ceux qui doivent être emmenés prisonniers seront emmenés. Et ceux qui doivent être tués à la guerre seront tués à la guerre.

sw.L: Naye atakuja na kuipiga nchi ya Misri: walio wa mauti, kwa mauti; na walio wa kufungwa, kwa kufungwa; na walio wa upanga, kwa upanga.
sw.B: Atakuja na kuipiga nchi ya Misri: aliyekusudiwa mauti, kwa mauti; aliyekusudiwa kuchukuliwa mateka, kwa kuchukuliwa mateka; na aliyekusudiwa upanga, kwa upanga.
sw.R: Atakuja na kuishambulia Misri. Wale waliopangiwa kufa watakufa. Wale waliopangiwa kuchukuliwa mateka watachukuliwa. Na wale waliopangiwa kuuawa vitani watauawa vitani.

vi.L: Nó sẽ đến và đánh xứ Ai Cập: ai phải chết thì chết, ai phải bị lưu đày thì bị lưu đày, ai phải bị gươm thì bị gươm.
vi.B: Nó sẽ đến và đánh xứ Ai Cập: ai đã định cho sự chết thì phải chết, ai đã định cho cảnh tù đày thì bị tù đày, ai đã định cho lưỡi gươm thì bị gươm giết.
vi.R: Nó sẽ đến tấn công Ai Cập. Ai phải chết thì sẽ chết. Ai phải bị bắt làm tù binh thì sẽ bị bắt. Ai phải bị giết trong chiến tranh thì sẽ bị giết.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 와서 이집트 땅을 칠 것이다. 죽음에 [처할] 자는 죽음으로, 포로가 [될] 자는 포로로, 칼에 [맞을] 자는 칼로 [갈 것이다].
ko.B: 그가 와서 이집트 땅을 칠 것이다. 죽기로 정해진 사람은 죽고, 포로가 되기로 정해진 사람은 포로가 되고, 칼에 맞기로 정해진 사람은 칼에 맞을 것이다.
ko.R: 그가 와서 이집트를 공격할 것이다. 죽을 사람은 죽을 것이다. 포로로 끌려갈 사람은 끌려갈 것이다. 전쟁에서 죽을 사람은 전쟁에서 죽을 것이다.

pt.L: E ele virá e ferirá a terra do Egito: os [que são] para a morte, para a morte; e os [que são] para o cativeiro, para o cativeiro; e os [que são] para a espada, para a espada.
pt.B: Ele virá e ferirá a terra do Egito: quem está destinado à morte, para a morte; quem está destinado ao cativeiro, para o cativeiro; e quem está destinado à espada, para a espada.
pt.R: Ele virá e atacará o Egito. Os que estão destinados a morrer vão morrer. Os que estão destinados a ser levados como prisioneiros vão ser levados. E os que estão destinados a morrer na guerra vão morrer na guerra.

decisions.choice: those for death, to death: the saying first spoken against Judah in 15:2
decisions.reason: Each group goes to the fate set for it, and no one escapes. The words once spoken over Jerusalem now fall on Egypt, the land the people thought would be safe (42:16-17).

decisions.choice: death: probably death by disease, set beside captivity and the sword
decisions.reason: As in 15:2, next to the sword "death" most likely means death by plague.

decisions.choice: he will come: the reading the scribes' tradition gives for this word
decisions.reason: The written letters of the Hebrew can be taken as "she will come", and the margin directs that the word be read "he will come", which fits Nebuchadrezzar as the subject. This is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: attack; killed in war
decisions.reason: As in 15:2, Readable turns the short verbless phrases into sentences and says "war" for the sword.

decisions.choice: "죽음에 [처할] 자는 죽음으로 ... [갈 것이다]" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean cannot keep the bare Hebrew pairs; Literal brackets the verbs the saying implies, the same wording as 15:2.

source.text: וְהִצַּ֣תִּי אֵ֗שׁ בְּבָתֵּי֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י מִצְרַ֔יִם וּשְׂרָפָ֖ם וְשָׁבָ֑ם וְעָטָה֩ אֶת־אֶ֨רֶץ מִצְרַ֜יִם כַּאֲשֶׁר־יַעְטֶ֤ה הָֽרֹעֶה֙ אֶת־בִּגְד֔וֹ וְיָצָ֥א מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will kindle fire in [the] houses of [the] gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and take them captive; and he will wrap [the] land of Egypt as wraps the shepherd his garment, and he will go out from there in peace.

en.L: And I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and take them captive; and he will wrap [himself in] the land of Egypt as the shepherd wraps [himself in] his garment, and he will go out from there in peace.
en.B: I will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and carry them off as captives. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will leave there unharmed.
en.R: I will set fire to the temples of Egypt's gods. Nebuchadrezzar will burn the gods or carry them off as captives. He will wrap the land of Egypt around himself as easily as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak. Then he will leave there safely.

es.L: Y prenderé fuego a las casas de los dioses de Egipto, y él las quemará y se los llevará cautivos; y se envolverá [en] la tierra de Egipto como el pastor se envuelve [en] su manto, y saldrá de allí en paz.
es.B: Prenderé fuego a los templos de los dioses de Egipto, y él los quemará y se llevará cautivos a los dioses. Se envolverá en la tierra de Egipto como un pastor se envuelve en su manto, y saldrá de allí sin daño.
es.R: Prenderé fuego a los templos de los dioses de Egipto. Nabucodorosor quemará a los dioses o se los llevará como prisioneros. Se envolverá con la tierra de Egipto tan fácilmente como un pastor se envuelve en su manto. Luego se irá de allí sin problemas.

fr.L: Et j’allumerai un feu dans les maisons des dieux de l’Égypte, et il les brûlera et les emmènera captifs ; et il s’enveloppera du pays d’Égypte comme le berger s’enveloppe de son vêtement, et il sortira de là en paix.
fr.B: Je mettrai le feu aux temples des dieux de l’Égypte ; il les brûlera et emmènera les dieux en captivité. Il s’enveloppera du pays d’Égypte comme un berger s’enveloppe de son manteau, et il repartira de là sans dommage.
fr.R: Je mettrai le feu aux temples des dieux de l’Égypte. Nabuchodonosor brûlera les dieux ou les emmènera comme des prisonniers. Il s’enveloppera du pays d’Égypte aussi facilement qu’un berger s’enveloppe de son manteau. Puis il repartira de là sain et sauf.

sw.L: Nami nitawasha moto katika nyumba za miungu ya Misri, naye ataziteketeza na kuwachukua mateka; naye ataivaa nchi ya Misri kama mchungaji avaavyo vazi lake, naye atatoka huko kwa amani.
sw.B: Nitawasha moto katika mahekalu ya miungu ya Misri, naye atayateketeza na kuichukua miungu yao mateka. Ataivaa nchi ya Misri kama mchungaji ajifunikavyo kwa joho lake, naye ataondoka huko salama.
sw.R: Nitawasha moto katika mahekalu ya miungu ya Misri. Nebukadreza ataichoma miungu hiyo au kuichukua mateka. Ataifunga nchi ya Misri mwilini mwake kwa urahisi kama mchungaji ajifunikavyo kwa joho lake. Kisha ataondoka huko salama.

vi.L: Ta sẽ châm lửa đốt các đền của các thần Ai Cập, nó sẽ đốt chúng và bắt chúng đi; nó sẽ quấn xứ Ai Cập [quanh mình] như người chăn chiên quấn áo mình, và nó sẽ ra khỏi đó bình an.
vi.B: Ta sẽ phóng hỏa các đền thờ của các thần Ai Cập, và nó sẽ đốt các thần ấy hoặc bắt chúng đem đi. Nó sẽ khoác lấy xứ Ai Cập như người chăn chiên khoác áo choàng, rồi ra đi bình an vô sự.
vi.R: Ta sẽ phóng hỏa các đền thờ của các thần Ai Cập. Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa sẽ đốt các thần ấy hoặc bắt chúng đem đi. Nó sẽ khoác lấy xứ Ai Cập dễ dàng như người chăn chiên khoác áo choàng. Rồi nó sẽ ra đi an toàn.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 이집트 신들의 집들에 불을 놓을 것이니, 그가 그것들을 불사르고 그것들을 사로잡아 갈 것이다. 그리고 목자가 자기 옷을 [몸에] 두르듯이 그가 이집트 땅을 [몸에] 두르고, 거기서 평안히 떠나갈 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 이집트 신들의 신전에 불을 지르겠다. 그러면 그가 신전들을 불사르고 그 신들을 포로로 끌고 갈 것이다. 목자가 겉옷을 몸에 두르듯이 그가 이집트 땅을 몸에 두르고, 아무 탈 없이 거기서 떠나갈 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 이집트 신들의 신전에 불을 지르겠다. 느부갓레살은 그 신들을 불태우거나 포로처럼 끌고 갈 것이다. 목자가 겉옷을 몸에 두르듯이, 그는 아주 쉽게 이집트 땅을 손에 넣을 것이다. 그러고 나서 그는 무사히 그곳을 떠날 것이다.

pt.L: E porei fogo nas casas dos deuses do Egito, e ele as queimará e os levará cativos; e ele se envolverá [com] a terra do Egito como o pastor se envolve [com] a sua capa, e sairá dali em paz.
pt.B: Porei fogo nos templos dos deuses do Egito, e ele os queimará e os levará como cativos. Ele se envolverá com a terra do Egito como um pastor se envolve com a sua capa, e sairá de lá sem nenhum dano.
pt.R: Vou pôr fogo nos templos dos deuses do Egito. Nabucodorosor vai queimar os deuses ou levá-los como prisioneiros. Ele vai se enrolar na terra do Egito tão facilmente como um pastor se enrola na sua capa. Depois vai sair de lá em segurança.

decisions.choice: I will kindle: the LORD himself starts the fire
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "I will kindle"; the Greek translation reads "he will kindle", making the king the subject throughout. As in verse 10, God speaks of the king's work as his own. The Hebrew is followed. This description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: burn them and take them captive: the gods of Egypt, that is, their images
decisions.reason: Conquerors burned the images of a defeated people's gods or carried them off as trophies (48:7; 49:3; Isaiah 46:1-2). "Them" could also be the temples, which are burned, but only the gods can be taken captive.

decisions.choice: wrap: he will wrap the land about himself as easily as a shepherd puts on his cloak
alternatives: he will pick the land of Egypt clean as a shepherd picks lice from his cloak
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to wrap or cover oneself (Psalm 104:2; Isaiah 59:17). The picture is of a quick and easy conquest. Some take the verb as a different word meaning "pick clean", as a shepherd picks the lice out of his cloak: the king would strip Egypt bare.

decisions.choice: go out from there in peace: leave unharmed
decisions.reason: He will go home safely, with no one able to stop him. "In peace" here means safe and unhurt (Genesis 28:21).

decisions.choice: houses of the gods (Literal), temples (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: A god's "house" is his temple.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar ... the gods ... as easily as
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, says who "them" are (m2) and spells out the point of the shepherd picture (m3).

decisions.choice: prenderé fuego (God as subject)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "I will kindle" (the Greek and some versions read "he"); every level keeps God as the one who starts the fire, as the English does.

decisions.choice: các đền (L); các đền thờ (B, R)
decisions.reason: "The houses of the gods" are their temples; Literal says "đền", the word for a house of a god, rather than "nhà", which would read as dwellings.

decisions.choice: "신들의 집들" (L); "신전" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "houses"; Balanced and Readable use the word for a temple of a god.

decisions.choice: Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt: "house of the sun", the city of the sun god, Heliopolis
decisions.reason: The name means "house of the sun". The words "in the land of Egypt" set it apart from the town of Beth-shemesh in Judah (1 Samuel 6:9-15). It is the city called On in Genesis 41:45, which the Greeks called Heliopolis, "sun city", the chief center of the worship of the sun god Ra.

decisions.choice: standing stones: the obelisks of the sun temple
decisions.reason: The word names stone pillars set up for worship (Exodus 23:24; 2 Kings 10:26-27). Heliopolis was famous for its tall obelisks dedicated to the sun.

decisions.choice: he will burn the houses of the gods: the threat of verse 12 repeated to close the message
decisions.reason: The message ends where verse 12 began. The gods of Egypt, in whom the people hoped for safety, cannot protect even their own temples.

decisions.choice: Heliopolis, the city of the sun (Readable); Beth-shemesh (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the city's better-known name and its meaning, so it is not confused with Beth-shemesh in Judah (m1).

decisions.choice: standing stones (Literal), sacred pillars (Balanced), tall stone pillars (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level shows that these were stones set up for worship.

decisions.choice: Heliópolis, la ciudad del sol
decisions.reason: Beth-shemesh, "house of the sun", is the Hebrew name of the Egyptian city the Greeks called Heliopolis; Readable gives the known name, as the English.
